text: Can you describe exactly how your leg was positioned when you were first discovered after the crash, and have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your foot?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Dislocation of the Right Hip.

Based on your history of a rear-end collision, immediate right groin pain, and abnormal leg positioning, I suspect your hip was forced into flexion and adduction, causing it to dislocate posteriorly. This is a medical emergency requiring urgent reduction to prevent nerve damage. Can you confirm if your right leg is currently rotated outward and if you are unable to move the leg voluntarily?
